playstyle: Hold the front line. Bind one enemy into your reach, raise the shield arc in front of the party, and punish anyone who walks past. You win by making the enemy fight on your ground, not by winning the damage race.

abilities.name: Shield Bash
effects: stagger 0.8 s
pushes the target 1.5 m back
counts as a weapon hit for Iron Tether and Purge of Bonds
abilities.notes: Fast opener with no wind-up: a reaction, not a plan. 40 damage plus 0.8 s of stagger for 5.0 s of cooldown.

abilities.name: Tower Sweep
effects: hits every target inside a 120 degree frontal arc out to 2.6 m
stagger 0.5 s
the arc is drawn on the ground while it runs
abilities.notes: 0.35 s wind-up, so it clears the 340 ms readable floor. Two enemies in a line are hit together.

abilities.name: Brace
effects: 25% damage reduction for 4.0 s
movement speed -30% for 4.0 s
cannot be interrupted while it runs
abilities.notes: The price of standing still: 25% less damage taken, 30% slower, 18.0 s cooldown.

abilities.name: Iron Tether
effects: roots the target for 1.0 s at the moment of the cast
forces the target to walk to the Templar at 3.0 m per second for 3.0 s
if the target arrives it is bound for 2.5 s: rooted and slowed 40%
the bind breaks on any knockback, on a dash, or when the Templar moves more than 4.0 m away
the line is drawn from the Templar to the target while it runs
abilities.notes: The real peel: the target is dragged into sword range instead of being snared where it stands. 9.0 m reach, 0.45 s cast, 14.0 s cooldown, 18 mana. Any knockback escapes it, so Cinder Burst and Cluster Shell both answer this.

abilities.name: Bulwark Arc
effects: a 120 degree frontal arc in front of the Templar, 5.0 m radius
for 6.0 s the arc absorbs 120 damage per hit from the front
blocked projectiles are stopped; melee attacks pass through the arc
the Templar takes 40% of the damage it absorbs
abilities.notes: The party shield is a cone on the ground, not a bubble around the Templar. It covers allies who stand inside it and it only faces one way: turn to face the archer.

abilities.name: Purge of Bonds
effects: clears one debuff from the Templar
clears one debuff from every ally inside 4.0 m
removes roots, stuns, silences and chills
does not remove damage over time, and does not heal
abilities.notes: The short cooldown anti-lock answer: 6.0 s, 12 mana, 0.25 s cast. It beats one stunlock cycle, not the whole class.

abilities.name: Phalanx Call
effects: every ally inside 6.0 m takes 25% less damage for 5.0 s
allies inside move 15% slower while the buff runs
the circle is visible to the whole party, not only to the Templar
abilities.notes: Group tanking. 25% damage reduction for five allies standing still for five seconds.

abilities.name: Crushing Advance
effects: dashes up to 8.0 m to the target
roots the target for 1.2 s
stagger 1.0 s
knocks the target back 2.0 m
the Templar stops on the target, not past it
abilities.notes: 0.5 s charge tell before the dash. This is how the Templar closes 8.0 m and turns a runner into a prisoner.

abilities.name: Ash Bulwark
effects: absorbs 300 damage in total over 8.0 s
blocks one control effect completely while it runs
reflects 20% of blocked melee damage back at the attacker
abilities.notes: The big shield: 300 damage, one clean control block, 45.0 s cooldown. It is the answer to one assassin dive, not to a whole warband.

abilities.name: Judgement of Iron
effects: ground slam inside a 4.0 m circle at 6.0 m
stagger 1.5 s
knocks back 3.0 m
the knockback breaks any bind on the affected targets
abilities.notes: 0.6 s cast with a ground circle where it lands. It is also the Templar's answer to a standing aura: land it on the singer.

abilities.name: Hold the Line
effects: for 12.0 s the Templar cannot be forced to move
roots, knockbacks, pulls and binds on the Templar are ignored
allies inside 3.0 m move 20% faster
ends early on death
abilities.notes: The anchor of the warband: 12.0 s of immunity to forced movement, 90.0 s cooldown, 40 mana.

weakness: Distance. Iron Tether reaches 9.0 m and Bulwark Arc needs the enemy in front of the shield, so a ranged class that never walks in wins. A clean stealth opener (a 4x assassin strike) also lands before the arc is up: the Templar has no answer to a dive that starts on top of it.
